sources.title: Meta raises $15 billion in five-part US bond sale
Skyworks tumbles as sluggish smartphone market weighs on forecast
Australia's Canva to cut 22% of jobs as growth slows for first time in a decade
Canada's Suncor Energy tops quarterly profit estimates

stories.headline: Meta raises US$15 billion in five-part bond sale
stories.body: Reuters reported Meta Platforms is raising US$15 billion through a five-part US-dollar bond offering to fund AI infrastructure investments.
stories.analysis: Additional large technology bond issuance may compete for investor capital; pricing and duration are needed before inferring any Treasury-yield or corporate-spread impact.
stories.watch_next: Final tranche pricing, coupons, maturities and spreads over matched-maturity Treasuries.

stories.headline: Skyworks warns of smartphone weakness and guides below consensus
stories.body: Skyworks forecast first-quarter revenue and earnings below Wall Street expectations amid continued smartphone demand weakness. Reuters reported the stock fell more than 14% in extended trading; precise price-observation time was not established.
stories.analysis: Demand weakness in premium Android smartphones contrasts with AI datacentre strength; integration synergies are not yet achieved cash flow.
stories.watch_next: Actual first-quarter demand, gross margins, Qorvo integration and savings delivery.

stories.headline: Canva announces 1,271 job cuts as growth slows
stories.body: Australian design software company Canva announced 1,271 job cuts, approximately 22% of its workforce, after growth slowed for the first time in a decade.
stories.analysis: Company-specific hiring retrenchment highlights differentiation between software operating economics and capital-intensive AI hardware demand; not a national jobs data surprise.
stories.watch_next: Restructuring execution, renewal trends, remaining workforce capacity and margins.

stories.headline: Suncor beats quarterly profit estimates and raises dividend
stories.body: Suncor reported adjusted operating profit of C$3.97 a share against the C$3.28 LSEG estimate for the third quarter. It raised its quarterly dividend 10% to C$0.66 a share.
stories.analysis: Elevated oil and refining margins can improve integrated energy cash flows while increasing cost pressure elsewhere; a single quarter is not a forward oil-price forecast.
stories.watch_next: Dividend funding, realised refinery margins and next-quarter crude pricing.
